# Atomic authenticated subscription rotation — UNRUN

Only the protected local pipeline may execute these fixtures. No direct test command, database operation or provider call was performed while preparing them.

Load the full captured PG17 catalog (actual push_subscriptions, auth.users/users/profiles and notification_preferences schema/ACL), existing component 164000, then new component 164500. The predecessor body is guarded by `md5(prosrc)=2f40ec68f6cbdd2288c5dd2d313ca358`, not a differently formatted pg_get_functiondef hash. The new component belongs after 164000; original components are unchanged. A preexisting rotation_revision column/function/trigger refuses with P0001 `push_rotation_contract_already_exists`. Root owns complete-bundle runner and source binding integration.

`regression.sql` uses actual service_role and actual ownership/rotation functions. It runs inside a rollback transaction, permits replica mode only for synthetic user setup, and uses the real revision trigger for behavioral calls. The maximum-counter and beyond-JS-precision cases temporarily disable only that trigger to seed otherwise inaccessible boundaries, then restore it before calls. An AFTER INSERT failure injects the last-write refusal and demands complete subscription/preference snapshot equality, including revision rollback. Refusal assertions reject NULL. Service-only ACL is checked by real anonymous/authenticated calls even with forged service claims. These facts are authored requirements, not passing results.

`concurrency.spec` is a separate PostgreSQL isolationtester input, NOT implicitly executed by the SQL regression/full acceptance runner. It orders a captured A observation against B taking the old endpoint, an A→B→A transition, and B enrolling another endpoint on the same recorded device. Rotation waits on the same advisory lock as enrollment, then must refuse without a new endpoint. The last case preserves the existing cross-account device collision for investigation; rotation does not decide who owns that device. A protected harness must bind the real isolationtester provider, assert expected waiting/completion and retain logs; no fabricated golden output is supplied.

The row-local revision starts at 1 on new INSERT and increments every UPDATE regardless of a caller-supplied value. It can conservatively refuse rotation after unrelated telemetry. It is not an installation epoch, past-ownership proof or revocation of an in-flight provider message. The route's text-cast PostgREST projection additionally needs an actual typed adapter qualification; native SQL alone does not establish JSON transport precision.

The World Hub route now requires a verified request actor and old key proof; sessionless worker calls are refused without any write. Foreground authenticated enrollment/replacement remains recovery. Background automatic rotation is still missing client-held account binding; the existing foreground sync has account/throttle limitations. Delayed requests that themselves obtain a different account's valid authentication, session revocation after API verification, stale dispatcher writes, provider-accepted messages, and authenticated per-device display acknowledgments remain out of scope and unqualified. No financial, invoice or social message formatting changes are made here.
